messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Ruby on Rails application. Start in the `/app` Git repository. It has no app yet. Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, the gems of a default `rails new` app, SQLite, and Chromium are installed. You can install other gems from rubygems.org; other network access is blocked. Install all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Moderators started asking for this:

> As a moderator, I want to reuse my quiz at another conference, or share it with a colleague who runs Quizzy too.

The quiz page gets the "Export" link. It opens a page that shows the quiz as JSON inside a `<pre>` element (the only `<pre>` on the page), ready to copy.

`/moderate` gets the "Import quiz" button. It opens a page with a "Quiz JSON" text area and the "Import" button. Importing always creates a new quiz, even if a quiz with the same title exists, and opens its page.

The format:

```json
{
  "title": "Frontend Fest 2026",
  "questions": [
    {
      "text": "Which HTTP status code means \"Too Many Requests\"?",
      "active": true,
      "options": [
        {"text": "418", "correct": false},
        {"text": "429", "correct": true}
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

- `questions` and `options` keep their order.
- On import, `active` is optional (`true` by default), and `correct` is optional (`false` by default).
- The export always writes both, and it writes exactly these keys: the quiz title and its questions, nothing else. The export is only for moving quiz contents.
- Imported questions follow the same rules as the question form.

When the JSON is invalid or breaks a rule, the page shows an error and nothing is imported: not the quiz, not a part of its questions.

--- README
# Quizzy

A live quiz app for conference talks. The moderator prepares quizzes on the
moderator side (`/moderate`); the audience side comes later.

## Run it

```sh
RAILS_ENV=production PORT=3000 \
SECRET_KEY_BASE=... \
QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME=... \
QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD=... \
bin/serve
```

`bin/serve` prepares the databases (under `storage/`) and the assets, then runs the
app in the foreground on all interfaces. `GET /up` returns 200 when the app is ready.

Every page under `/moderate` asks for the moderator's HTTP Basic credentials.

## Develop and test

```sh
bundle install
bin/rails db:prepare
bin/rails test                       # unit and request tests
bin/rails test:system                # all browser tests (Cuprite + headless Chromium)
bin/rails test test/system/layout_test.rb   # one browser test file
bin/rubocop
bin/brakeman
```

For the browser tests, `BROWSER_PATH` points at Chromium (default `/usr/bin/chromium`).

Design notes, mockups and the reasoning behind decisions live in `docs/`.

--- README
# Quizzy

A live quiz app for conference talks. The moderator prepares quizzes on the
moderator side (`/moderate`); the audience side comes later.

## Run it

```sh
RAILS_ENV=production PORT=3000 \
SECRET_KEY_BASE=... \
QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME=... \
QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD=... \
bin/serve
```

`bin/serve` prepares the databases (under `storage/`) and the assets, then runs the
app in the foreground on all interfaces. `GET /up` returns 200 when the app is ready.

Every page under `/moderate` asks for the moderator's HTTP Basic credentials.

## Develop and test

```sh
bundle install
bin/rails db:prepare
bin/rails test                       # unit and request tests
bin/rails test:system                # all browser tests (Cuprite + headless Chromium)
bin/rails test test/system/layout_test.rb   # one browser test file
bin/rubocop
bin/brakeman
```

For the browser tests, `BROWSER_PATH` points at Chromium (default `/usr/bin/chromium`).

Design notes, mockups and the reasoning behind decisions live in `docs/`.

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# Quizzy: design notes

Living notes for the next steps. The design itself lives in `docs/mockups/`
(style guide, quiz page, question form; `quizzy.css` and the Inter font are the
design's assets). This file records what we built and why.

## Scope of this release

The moderator side only:

- quizzes (list, create, settings, delete)
- questions with text options, ordering, activation, delete
- the preview: a player-style run through the active questions

Not built yet: player pages (join, answer on phones), big-screen pages, live
responses, leaderboards. The design CSS already contains their classes.

## Running

`bin/serve` is the only entry point. With `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT`,
`SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`
set, it:

1. checks the variables (exits if one is missing),
2. checks the bundle is satisfied from the local gems (`bundle install --local` as
   fallback, never the network),
3. runs `db:prepare` (creates and migrates every production SQLite database),
4. runs `assets:precompile` into `public/assets`,
5. `exec`s `rails server` on `0.0.0.0:$PORT` in the foreground.

Data lives only under `storage/`: `production.sqlite3` (app), plus the Solid
Cache, Queue and Cable databases. Logs go to STDOUT. `GET /up` is the health check.

## Routes

| Path | Screen |
| --- | --- |
| `/` | redirects to `/moderate` |
| `/moderate` | quiz list, "New quiz" |
| `/moderate/quizzes/new` | quiz form (Title, "Save quiz") |
| `/moderate/quizzes/:id` | quiz page: questions, "Add question", "Settings", "Preview" |
| `/moderate/quizzes/:id/edit` | "Settings": same quiz form, "Delete quiz" (confirm) |
| `/moderate/quizzes/:id/preview` | player-style run of the active questions |
| `/moderate/quizzes/:id/questions/new` | question form |
| `/moderate/quizzes/:id/questions/:id/edit` | question form, pre-filled |
| `PATCH .../questions/:id/move_up`, `move_down` | reorder |
| `PATCH .../questions/:id/activation` | the "Active" switch on the quiz page (saves at once) |

Everything under `/moderate` requires HTTP Basic auth (`Moderate::BaseController`).
The check runs before CSRF verification (`prepend_before_action`), so anonymous
POSTs get 401, not 422.

## Domain rules

- Quiz: `title` required (trimmed, max 200).
- Question: `text` required (trimmed). `active` defaults to true. `position` puts
  new questions last; "Move up/down" swaps with the neighbour among *all*
  questions, active or not, and renumbers positions 1..n.
- Options are edited as rows (`question[options][N][text]`,
  `question[options][N][correct]`). Rules, checked before anything is written:
  - rows whose text is blank (after trimming) are skipped, even if marked correct;
  - fewer than two remaining rows: "Add at least two options";
  - none of the remaining rows correct: "Mark at least one option as correct";
  - several correct options are fine.
  Both messages can show together. A failed save writes nothing and re-renders
  the form with the typed rows, the checkboxes and the Active state.
- A successful save replaces the question's options in the same transaction.
- Quiz page numbering: active questions are numbered 1, 2, ... and inactive ones
  show "—". Inactive questions keep their place and are dimmed.

## Preview (stateless)

- The run lives only in the URL: `results` is one character per answered
  question (`1` correct, `0` wrong), `pick` is the option chosen on the current
  question. Nothing is written to the database or the session. Reloading or
  "Start over" (no parameters) restarts it.
- Picking an option renders the feedback: "Correct!" or "Wrong!", the correct
  options revealed, and "Next question" (or "See score" on the last one) carrying
  the new `results`.
- The score page shows "Score: X/Y". Only active questions are played.
- Logic lives in `QuizPreview` (plain Ruby, unit-tested).

## Labels the QA tests rely on

These strings are exact (visible text, `<label>`, placeholder or aria-label):

- Buttons: "New quiz", "Save quiz", "Add question", "Delete quiz", "Add option",
  "Save question", "Move up", "Move down", "Delete", "Next question",
  "See score", "Start over". Navigation buttons are real `<button>`s
  (`button_to` with GET), not links.
- Links: "Settings", "Preview", "Edit".
- Fields: "Title", "Question", "Option N" (text), "Option N is correct"
  (checkbox), "Active" (checkbox, quiz page and question form).
- Messages: "Add at least two options", "Mark at least one option as correct",
  "Title can't be blank", "Question can't be blank", "Question 1 of 3",
  "Correct!", "Wrong!", "Score: 2/3".

Insight: the mockups use icon-only buttons (↑ ↓ ✕). Labels stay visible as text
("Move up", "Move down"); the ✕ row remover has an `aria-label` only.

## Front end

- `quizzy.css` is the design file, unchanged. App-specific rules are in
  `app/assets/stylesheets/moderator.css`.
- Propshaft resolves `url()` relative to the CSS file, so the font sits next to
  `quizzy.css`.
- Turbo Drive handles forms. Delete confirmations use `data-turbo-confirm`, which
  Turbo shows with the native `confirm()` dialog.
- `auto-submit` Stimulus controller: the Active switch submits its form on change.
- `option-rows` Stimulus controller: "Add option" appends a row built from a
  `<script type="text/template">` (kept out of the DOM tree so non-JS parsers
  never see its fields); removing a row renumbers the rest.
- Forms carry `required` but `novalidate`, so the browser leaves validation to the
  server messages.
- The option "✕" remover is an extra beyond the brief, from the mockup.

## Production setup insights

- Propshaft does not serve assets in production. `bin/serve` precompiles into
  `public/assets`, and `config.public_file_server` stays on (no proxy in front).
- The default Action Cable config used Redis. It is `solid_cable` on SQLite now,
  so nothing calls an external service.
- `allow_browser` was removed: player pages run on any phone browser.
- SSL is off (`force_ssl = false`, `assume_ssl = false`), and `config.hosts` is
  cleared so any host name is accepted.
- `config/master.key` and the credentials file are gone; secrets come from the
  environment only. `/config/master.key` is gitignored anyway.
- Gems: `Gemfile.lock` pins the versions preinstalled in the image, so the bundle
  resolves offline. For system tests, Cuprite drives the system Chromium
  (`BROWSER_PATH`, default `/usr/bin/chromium`) instead of Selenium.

## Testing

- `bin/rails test`: model rules, preview state, HTTP Basic access, request flows.
- `bin/rails test:system`: browser flows with Cuprite and headless Chromium
  (`test/system`). `bin/rails test test/system/<file>` runs one file. Basic auth
  is answered through Ferrum's `network.authorize`.
- `bin/rubocop` (omakase style), `bin/brakeman`.
- No network needed for any of it.
"
}

- `bin/rails test`: model rules, preview state, HTTP Basic access, request flows.
- `bin/rails test:system`: browser flows with Cuprite and headless Chromium
  (`test/system`). `bin/rails test test/system/<file>` runs one file. Basic auth
  is answered through Ferrum's `network.authorize`.
- `bin/rubocop` (omakase style), `bin/brakeman`.
- No network needed for any of it.

class ApplicationRecord < ActiveRecord::Base
  primary_abstract_class

class Option < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :question, inverse_of: :options

  validates :text, presence: true
end
# A single-choice question with text options.
#
# Options are edited as "rows" (see #option_rows=). Rows with blank text are
# skipped. A question needs at least two options and at least one of them must
# be correct. Rules are checked before anything is written; the options are
# replaced in the same transaction as the question.
class Question < ApplicationRecord
  MIN_OPTIONS = 2
  FORM_OPTION_ROWS = 4

  belongs_to :quiz, inverse_of: :questions
  has_many :options, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :question

  scope :active, -> { where(active: true) }

  normalizes :text, with: ->(text) { text.strip }

  validates :text, presence: true
  validate :validate_option_rows, if: -> { @option_rows }

  before_create :place_at_end
  after_save :save_option_rows, if: -> { @option_rows }

  # Rows as typed in the form: [{ text:, correct: }, ...], in display order.
  # Assigning rows does not touch the database until the question is saved.
  attr_reader :option_rows

  def option_rows=(rows)
    @option_rows = Array(rows).map do |row|
      { text: row[:text].to_s, correct: ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new.cast(row[:correct]) == true }
    end
  end

  # Rows to show in the form: what was typed, or the saved options, padded to
  # FORM_OPTION_ROWS so the form always has room for new options.
  def form_option_rows
    rows = @option_rows || options.map { |option| { text: option.text, correct: option.correct } }
    rows + Array.new([ FORM_OPTION_ROWS - rows.size, 0 ].max) { { text: "", correct: false } }
  end

  def move_up
    move_by(-1)
  end

  def move_down
    move_by(1)
  end

  private

  def kept_option_rows
    (@option_rows || []).select { |row| row[:text].strip.present? }
  end

  def validate_option_rows
    kept = kept_option_rows
    errors.add(:base, "Add at least two options") if kept.size < MIN_OPTIONS
    errors.add(:base, "Mark at least one option as correct") if kept.none? { |row| row[:correct] }
  end

  def save_option_rows
    Option.where(question_id: id).delete_all
    kept_option_rows.each.with_index(1) do |row, position|
      Option.create!(question: self, text: row[:text].strip, correct: row[:correct], position: position)
    end
    @option_rows = nil
    options.reset
  end

  def place_at_end
    self.position = quiz.questions.maximum(:position).to_i + 1
  end

  def move_by(step)
    ordered = quiz.questions.reorder(:position, :id).to_a
    index = ordered.index { |question| question.id == id }
    target = index && index + step
    return if index.nil? || target.negative? || target >= ordered.size

    ordered[index], ordered[target] = ordered[target], ordered[index]
    Question.transaction do
      ordered.each.with_index(1) do |question, position|
        question.update_column(:position, position) unless question.position == position
      end
    end
    reload
  end
end
class Quiz < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :quiz

  normalizes :title, with: ->(title) { title.strip }

end
# One "play it as a player" run through a quiz's active questions.
#
# Nothing is stored: the whole run travels in the URL. `results` holds one
# character per answered question ("1" correct, "0" wrong), and `pick` is the
# option chosen for the question on screen, if any.
class QuizPreview
  attr_reader :questions

  def initialize(questions, results: nil, pick: nil)
    @questions = questions.to_a
    @results = results.to_s.delete("^01")[0, @questions.size]
    @pick = pick.to_s
  end

  def total
    questions.size
  end

  def empty?
    questions.empty?
  end

  def answered
    @results.length
  end

  def results
    @results
  end

  def finished?
    !empty? && answered >= total
  end

  def score
    @results.count("1")
  end

  def current_question
    questions[answered] unless empty? || finished?
  end

  def last_question?
    answered + 1 == total
  end

  def picked_option
    return unless current_question && @pick.present?

    current_question.options.find { |option| option.id.to_s == @pick }
  end

  def revealed?
    picked_option.present?
  end

  def correct_pick?
    picked_option&.correct? || false
  end

  # The results string once the question on screen is answered.
  def results_with_answer
    @results + (correct_pick? ? "1" : "0")
  end
end

module Moderate
  # Everything under /moderate needs the moderator's HTTP Basic credentials.
  class BaseController < ApplicationController
    # Runs before the CSRF check, so anonymous requests always get a 401.
    prepend_before_action :require_moderator

    private

    def require_moderator
      authenticate_or_request_with_http_basic("Quizzy moderator") do |username, password|
        moderator_credentials?(username, password)
      end
    end

    def moderator_credentials?(username, password)
      expected_username = ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME"].to_s
      expected_password = ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD"].to_s
      return false if expected_username.empty? || expected_password.empty?

      ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare(username.to_s, expected_username) &&
        ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare(password.to_s, expected_password)
    end
  end

module Moderate
  class QuestionsController < BaseController
    before_action :set_quiz
    before_action :set_question, except: %i[new create]

    def new
      @question = @quiz.questions.new(active: true)
    end

    def create
      @question = @quiz.questions.new(question_params)
      @question.option_rows = option_rows_params
      if @question.save
        redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(@quiz, anchor: helpers.dom_id(@question)), notice: "Question saved."
      else
        render :new, status: :unprocessable_entity
      end
    end

    def edit
    end

    def update
      @question.assign_attributes(question_params)
      @question.option_rows = option_rows_params
      if @question.save
        redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(@quiz, anchor: helpers.dom_id(@question)), notice: "Question saved."
      else
        render :edit, status: :unprocessable_entity
      end
    end

    def destroy
      @question.destroy
      redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(@quiz), notice: "Question deleted.", status: :see_other
    end

    def move_up
      @question.move_up
      redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(@quiz, anchor: helpers.dom_id(@question)), status: :see_other
    end

    def move_down
      @question.move_down
      redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(@quiz, anchor: helpers.dom_id(@question)), status: :see_other
    end

    # The "Active" switch on the quiz page: saves at once.
    def activation
      @question.update(active: params.require(:question).permit(:active)[:active])
      redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(@quiz, anchor: helpers.dom_id(@question)), status: :see_other
    end

    private

    def set_quiz
      @quiz = Quiz.find(params[:quiz_id])
    end

    def set_question
      @question = @quiz.questions.find(params[:id])
    end

    def question_params
      params.require(:question).permit(:text, :active)
    end

    # question[options][0][text], question[options][0][correct], question[options][1][text], ...
    # Rows come back in the order of their index, so the form order is kept.
    def option_rows_params
      options = params.dig(:question, :options)
      return [] unless options.respond_to?(:keys)

      options.keys.sort_by(&:to_i).filter_map do |key|
        row = options[key]
        next unless row.is_a?(ActionController::Parameters)

        { text: row[:text].to_s, correct: row[:correct] }
      end
    end
  end
end

      redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(@quiz, anchor: helpers.dom_id(@question)), status: :see_other
    end

    def move_down
      @question.move_down
      redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(@quiz, anchor: helpers.dom_id(@question)), status: :see_other
    end

    # The "Active" switch on the quiz page: saves at once.
    def activation
      @question.update(active: params.require(:question).permit(:active)[:active])
      redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(@quiz, anchor: helpers.dom_id(@question)), status: :see_other
    end

    private

    def set_quiz
      @quiz = Quiz.find(params[:quiz_id])
    end

    def set_question
      @question = @quiz.questions.find(params[:id])
    end

    def question_params
      params.require(:question).permit(:text, :active)
    end

    # question[options][0][text], question[options][0][correct], question[options][1][text], ...
    # Rows come back in the order of their index, so the form order is kept.
    def option_rows_params
      options = params.dig(:question, :options)
      return [] unless options.respond_to?(:keys)

      options.keys.sort_by(&:to_i).filter_map do |key|
        row = options[key]
        next unless row.is_a?(ActionController::Parameters)

        { text: row[:text].to_s, correct: row[:correct] }
      end
    end
  end
end

        render :new, status: :unprocessable_entity
      end

    end

      end

// Configure your import map in config/importmap.rb. Read more: https://github.com/rails/importmap-rails
import "@hotwired/turbo-rails"
import "controllers"
import { Application } from "@hotwired/stimulus"

const application = Application.start()

// Configure Stimulus development experience
application.debug = false
window.Stimulus   = application

export { application }
import { Controller } from "@hotwired/stimulus"

// Saves the enclosing form as soon as one of its fields changes (used for switches).
export default class extends Controller {
  submit() {
    this.element.requestSubmit()
  }
}
// Import and register all your controllers from the importmap via controllers/**/*_controller
import { application } from "controllers/application"
import { eagerLoadControllersFrom } from "@hotwired/stimulus-loading"
eagerLoadControllersFrom("controllers", application)
import { Controller } from "@hotwired/stimulus"

// Adds, removes and renumbers the option rows of a question form.
// Each row posts question[options][N][text] and question[options][N][correct],
// where N is the row's position on the page.
export default class extends Controller {
  static targets = ["list", "row", "template"]

  add(event) {
    event.preventDefault()
    this.listTarget.insertAdjacentHTML("beforeend", this.templateTarget.textContent)
    this.renumber()

    const rows = this.rowTargets
    rows[rows.length - 1].querySelector("[data-role='text']").focus()
  }

  remove(event) {
    event.preventDefault()
    event.currentTarget.closest(".option-row").remove()
    this.renumber()
  }

  renumber() {
    this.rowTargets.forEach((row, index) => {
      const number = index + 1
      const textId = `question_options_${index}_text`
      const correctId = `question_options_${index}_correct`

      const label = row.querySelector("[data-role='label']")
      label.textContent = `Option ${number}`
      label.htmlFor = textId

      const text = row.querySelector("[data-role='text']")
      text.id = textId
      text.name = `question[options][${index}][text]`

      const correct = row.querySelector("[data-role='correct']")
      correct.id = correctId
      correct.name = `question[options][${index}][correct]`

      row.querySelector("[data-role='correct-label']").textContent = `Option ${number} is correct`
      row.querySelector("[data-role='remove']").setAttribute("aria-label", `Remove option ${number}`)
    })
  }
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Quizzy: prepare the app and run it in production mode, in the foreground.
#
#   RAILS_ENV=production PORT=3000 SECRET_KEY_BASE=... \
#   QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME=... QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD=... bin/serve
#
# Everything the app needs lives under storage/ (SQLite databases) and
# public/assets (precompiled files). Nothing here talks to external services.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export RAILS_ENV="${RAILS_ENV:-production}"
export PORT="${PORT:-3000}"

for name in SECRET_KEY_BASE QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD; do
  if [ -z "${!name:-}" ]; then
    echo "bin/serve: $name must be set" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done

# Gems come from the local installation; resolving them must not need the network.
bundle check >/dev/null 2>&1 || bundle install --local

mkdir -p storage tmp/pids log
rm -f tmp/pids/server.pid

bin/rails db:prepare
bin/rails assets:precompile

exec bin/rails server --environment "$RAILS_ENV" --binding 0.0.0.0 --port "$PORT" --pid tmp/pids/server.pid

eagerLoadControllersFrom("controllers", application)
import { Controller } from "@hotwired/stimulus"

// Adds, removes and renumbers the option rows of a question form.
// Each row posts question[options][N][text] and question[options][N][correct],
// where N is the row's position on the page.
export default class extends Controller {
  static targets = ["list", "row", "template"]

  add(event) {
    event.preventDefault()
    this.listTarget.insertAdjacentHTML("beforeend", this.templateTarget.textContent)
    this.renumber()

    const rows = this.rowTargets
    rows[rows.length - 1].querySelector("[data-role='text']").focus()
  }

  remove(event) {
    event.preventDefault()
    event.currentTarget.closest(".option-row").remove()
    this.renumber()
  }

  renumber() {
    this.rowTargets.forEach((row, index) => {
      const number = index + 1
      const textId = `question_options_${index}_text`
      const correctId = `question_options_${index}_correct`

      const label = row.querySelector("[data-role='label']")
      label.textContent = `Option ${number}`
      label.htmlFor = textId

      const text = row.querySelector("[data-role='text']")
      text.id = textId
      text.name = `question[options][${index}][text]`

      const correct = row.querySelector("[data-role='correct']")
      correct.id = correctId
      correct.name = `question[options][${index}][correct]`

      row.querySelector("[data-role='correct-label']").textContent = `Option ${number} is correct`
      row.querySelector("[data-role='remove']").setAttribute("aria-label", `Remove option ${number}`)
    })
  }
}

# Quizzy: prepare the app and run it in production mode, in the foreground.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export RAILS_ENV="${RAILS_ENV:-production}"
export PORT="${PORT:-3000}"

for name in SECRET_KEY_BASE QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD; do
  if [ -z "${!name:-}" ]; then
    echo "bin/serve: $name must be set" >&2

bundle check >/dev/null 2>&1 || bundle install --local

  test "inactive questions keep their place in the order" do
    a = make_question("a")

  private

  end

  def build_question(option_rows, active: true)
    question = @quiz.questions.new(text: "Question?", active: active)

  def make_question(text, active: true)
    question = build_question(rows([ [ "A", true ], [ "B", false ] ]), active: active)

  end

    @quiz.questions.reload.map(&:text)

require "test_helper"

class QuizPreviewTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Talk")
    @questions = 3.times.map do |i|
      question = quiz.questions.new(text: "Q#{i + 1}", active: true)
      question.option_rows = [ { text: "right", correct: true }, { text: "wrong", correct: false } ]
      question.save!
      question
    end
  end

  test "starts at the first question" do
    preview = QuizPreview.new(@questions)
    assert_equal "Q1", preview.current_question.text
    assert_equal 0, preview.answered
    assert_not preview.revealed?
    assert_not preview.finished?
  end

  test "a pick reveals the answer and carries the result forward" do
    right = @questions.first.options.find_by!(text: "right")
    preview = QuizPreview.new(@questions, pick: right.id)
    assert preview.revealed?
    assert preview.correct_pick?
    assert_equal "1", preview.results_with_answer
  end

  test "results count answered questions and score the right ones" do
    preview = QuizPreview.new(@questions, results: "101")
    assert preview.finished?
    assert_equal 2, preview.score
    assert_nil preview.current_question
  end

  test "garbage in the results is ignored" do
    preview = QuizPreview.new(@questions, results: "x1y0z9")
    assert_equal "10", preview.results
    assert_equal "Q3", preview.current_question.text
  end

  test "an unknown or foreign pick is not an answer" do
    other = Quiz.create!(title: "Other")
    question = other.questions.new(text: "Foreign", active: true)
    question.option_rows = [ { text: "a", correct: true }, { text: "b", correct: false } ]
    question.save!
    foreign = question.options.first

    assert_not QuizPreview.new(@questions, pick: foreign.id).revealed?
    assert_not QuizPreview.new(@questions, pick: "nope").revealed?
  end

  test "an empty quiz has nothing to play" do
    preview = QuizPreview.new([])
    assert preview.empty?
    assert_not preview.finished?
    assert_nil preview.current_question
  end
end

    assert_selector ".question-item", text: "Typed question"
    assert_equal %w[Only\ one Second], quiz.questions.first.options.map(&:text)
    assert_equal [ false, true ], quiz.questions.first.options.map(&:correct)
  end

  test "moving questions changes their order" do
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Talk")
    first = create_question(quiz, "First question")
    create_question(quiz, "Second question")

    visit "/moderate/quizzes/#{quiz.id}"
    assert_equal [ "First question", "Second question" ], question_texts

    within(".question-item", text: "Second question") { click_button "Move up" }
    assert_equal [ "Second question", "First question" ], question_texts

    within(".question-item", text: "Second question") { click_button "Move down" }
    assert_equal [ "First question", "Second question" ], question_texts
    assert first.reload.position < Question.find_by!(text: "Second question").position
  end

  test "the active switch saves at once and inactive questions are dimmed" do
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Talk")
    question = create_question(quiz, "Switch me")

    visit "/moderate/quizzes/#{quiz.id}"
    within(".question-item", text: "Switch me") { uncheck "Active" }
    assert_selector ".question-item--inactive", text: "Switch me"
    assert_not question.reload.active?

    within(".question-item", text: "Switch me") { check "Active" }
    assert_no_selector ".question-item--inactive"
    assert question.reload.active?
  end

  test "deleting a question asks first" do
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Talk")
    create_question(quiz, "Keep me")
    create_question(quiz, "Delete me")

    visit "/moderate/quizzes/#{quiz.id}"
    dismiss_confirm("Delete this question?") do
      within(".question-item", text: "Delete me") { click_button "Delete" }
    end
    assert_text "Delete me"
    assert_equal 2, quiz.questions.count

    accept_confirm("Delete this question?") do
      within(".question-item", text: "Delete me") { click_button "Delete" }
    end
    assert_no_text "Delete me"
    assert_equal [ "Keep me" ], quiz.questions.reload.map(&:text)
  end

  test "deleting a quiz asks first and then goes back to the list" do
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Doomed")
    visit "/moderate/quizzes/#{quiz.id}/edit"
    dismiss_confirm { click_button "Delete quiz" }
    assert_equal 1, Quiz.where(id: quiz.id).count

    accept_confirm { click_button "Delete quiz" }
    assert_current_path "/moderate", ignore_query: true
    assert_no_text "Doomed"
    assert_equal 0, Quiz.where(id: quiz.id).count
  end

  private

  def question_texts
    page.all(".question-item__body").map(&:text)
  end

  def create_question(quiz, text)
    quiz.questions.create!(text: text, active: true).tap do |question|
      question.option_rows = [ { text: "A", correct: true }, { text: "B", correct: false } ]
      question.save!
    end
  end
end

My plan:

- **Import**: `GET /moderate/import/new` with a "Quiz JSON" textarea and an "Import" button, and `POST /moderate/import`. `/moderate` gets an "Import quiz" button. A `QuizImport` class checks the whole document first, reuses the `Question` model rules for each question, and saves the quiz and questions in one transaction.

# The JSON behind a quiz's "Export" page. It holds exactly the quiz title and
# its questions with their options, in their order: no ids, no timestamps.
# QuizImport reads this format back.
class QuizExport
  def initialize(quiz)
    @quiz = quiz
  end

  def to_h
    {
      title: @quiz.title,
      questions: @quiz.questions.includes(:options).map do |question|
        {
          text: question.text,
          active: question.active,
          options: question.options.map { |option| { text: option.text, correct: option.correct } }
        }
      end
    }
  end

  def pretty_json
    JSON.pretty_generate(to_h)
  end
end
EOF
cat > app/models/quiz_import.rb <<'EOF'
# Creates a brand-new quiz from the JSON that QuizExport writes ("Import quiz").
# An import always creates a quiz, even if one with the same title exists.
#
# Format (keys other than these are ignored):
#
#   { "title": "...",
#     "questions": [ { "text": "...", "active": true,
#                      "options": [ { "text": "...", "correct": false } ] } ] }
#
# "active" defaults to true and "correct" to false; null counts as missing.
#
# The whole document is checked before anything is written, and the quiz and its
# questions are saved in one transaction. A document that breaks a rule creates
# nothing: not the quiz, not part of its questions. Each question is checked by
# the same model rules as the question form (Question#option_rows).
class QuizImport
  include ActiveModel::Model

  attr_accessor :json
  attr_reader :quiz

  validate :check_document

  def save
    return false unless valid?

    Quiz.transaction do
      @quiz = Quiz.create!(title: @title)
      @questions.each do |draft|
        question = @quiz.questions.new(text: draft[:text], active: draft[:active])
        question.option_rows = draft[:options]
        question.save!
      end
    end
    true
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid => error
    # The checks below use the same rules, so this is a safety net only.
    @quiz = nil
    errors.add(:base, error.record.errors.full_messages.to_sentence)
    false
  end

  private

  def check_document
    @title = nil
    @questions = []

    document = read_document
    return unless document

    check_title(document["title"])
    check_questions(document["questions"])
  end

  def read_document
    if json.blank?
      errors.add(:json, :blank)
      return
    end

    document = JSON.parse(json)
    return document if document.is_a?(Hash)

    errors.add(:json, "must be an object with \"title\" and \"questions\"")
    nil
  rescue JSON::ParserError
    errors.add(:json, "is not valid JSON")
    nil
  end

  def check_title(value)
    if value.nil? || value.is_a?(String)
      @title = value.to_s
      # Same rules as the quiz form: the probe has no questions, so only the title is checked.
      probe = Quiz.new(title: @title)
      probe.validate
      probe.errors.full_messages.each { |message| errors.add(:base, message) }
    else
      errors.add(:base, "Title must be a string")
    end
  end

  def check_questions(value)
    unless value.is_a?(Array)
      errors.add(:base, "Questions must be a list")
      return
    end

    value.each.with_index(1) { |data, number| check_question(data, number) }
  end

  def check_question(data, number)
    label = "Question #{number}"
    unless data.is_a?(Hash)
      errors.add(:base, "#{label} must be an object")
      return
    end

    text = data["text"]
    errors.add(:base, "#{label}: Question must be a string") unless text.nil? || text.is_a?(String)

    active = data["active"].nil? ? true : data["active"]
    errors.add(:base, "#{label}: Active must be true or false") unless [ true, false ].include?(active)

    options = check_options(data["options"], label)

    question = Quiz.new.questions.new(text: text.is_a?(String) ? text : "", active: active == true)
    question.option_rows = options
    question.valid?
    question.errors.full_messages.each { |message| errors.add(:base, "#{label}: #{message}") }

    @questions << { text: question.text, active: active == true, options: options }
  end

  # Returns the option rows as the form would send them: [{ text:, correct: }, ...].
  def check_options(value, label)
    unless value.is_a?(Array)
      errors.add(:base, "#{label}: Options must be a list")
      return []
    end

    value.each.with_index(1).filter_map do |option, number|
      unless option.is_a?(Hash)
        errors.add(:base, "#{label}, option #{number} must be an object")
        next
      end

      text = option["text"]
      errors.add(:base, "#{label}, option #{number}: Option text must be a string") unless text.nil? || text.is_a?(String)

      correct = option["correct"].nil? ? false : option["correct"]
      errors.add(:base, "#{label}, option #{number}: Correct must be true or false") unless [ true, false ].include?(correct)

      { text: text.is_a?(String) ? text : "", correct: correct == true }
    end
  end
end
EOF

cd /app && cat > app/models/quiz_import.rb <<'EOF'
# Creates a brand-new quiz from the JSON that QuizExport writes ("Import quiz").
# An import always creates a quiz, even if one with the same title exists.
#
# Format (keys other than these are ignored):
#
#   { "title": "...",
#     "questions": [ { "text": "...", "active": true,
#                      "options": [ { "text": "...", "correct": false } ] } ] }
#
# "active" defaults to true and "correct" to false; null counts as missing.
#
# The whole document is checked before anything is written, and the quiz and its
# questions are saved in one transaction. A document that breaks a rule creates
# nothing: not the quiz, not part of its questions. Each question is checked by
# the same model rules as the question form (Question#option_rows).
class QuizImport
  include ActiveModel::Model

  attr_accessor :json
  attr_reader :quiz

  validate :check_document

  def save
    return false unless valid?

    Quiz.transaction do
      @quiz = Quiz.create!(title: @title)
      @questions.each do |draft|
        question = @quiz.questions.new(text: draft[:text], active: draft[:active])
        question.option_rows = draft[:options]
        question.save!
      end
    end
    true
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid => error
    # The checks below use the same rules, so this is a safety net only.
    @quiz = nil
    errors.add(:base, error.record.errors.full_messages.to_sentence)
    false
  end

  private

  def check_document
    @title = nil
    @questions = []

    document = read_document
    return unless document

    check_title(document["title"])
    check_questions(document["questions"])
  end

  def read_document
    if json.blank?
      errors.add(:json, :blank)
      return
    end

    document = JSON.parse(json)
    return document if document.is_a?(Hash)

    errors.add(:json, "must be an object with \"title\" and \"questions\"")
    nil
  rescue JSON::ParserError
    errors.add(:json, "is not valid JSON")
    nil
  end

  def check_title(value)
    if value.nil? || value.is_a?(String)
      @title = value.to_s
      # Same rules as the quiz form. The probe has no questions, so only the title is checked.
      probe = Quiz.new(title: @title)
      probe.validate
      probe.errors.full_messages.each { |message| errors.add(:base, message) }
    else
      errors.add(:base, "Title must be a string")
    end
  end

  def check_questions(value)
    unless value.is_a?(Array)
      errors.add(:base, "Questions must be a list")
      return
    end

    value.each.with_index(1) { |data, number| check_question(data, number) }
  end

  def check_question(data, number)
    label = "Question #{number}"
    unless data.is_a?(Hash)
      errors.add(:base, "#{label} must be an object")
      return
    end

    errors_before = errors.size
    text = data["text"]
    errors.add(:base, "#{label}: Question must be a string") unless text.nil? || text.is_a?(String)

    active = data["active"].nil? ? true : data["active"]
    errors.add(:base, "#{label}: Active must be true or false") unless [ true, false ].include?(active)

    options = check_options(data["options"], label)

    # The rules (blank text, too few options, no correct one) only make sense once
    # every field has the right type, so they are checked after the type errors.
    return unless errors.size == errors_before

    question = Quiz.new.questions.new(text: text, active: active)
    question.option_rows = options
    question.valid?
    question.errors.full_messages.each { |message| errors.add(:base, "#{label}: #{message}") }

    @questions << { text: question.text, active: active, options: options }
  end

  # Returns the option rows as the form would send them: [{ text:, correct: }, ...].
  def check_options(value, label)
    unless value.is_a?(Array)
      errors.add(:base, "#{label}: Options must be a list")
      return []
    end

    value.each.with_index(1).filter_map do |option, number|
      unless option.is_a?(Hash)
        errors.add(:base, "#{label}, option #{number} must be an object")
        next
      end

      text = option["text"]
      errors.add(:base, "#{label}, option #{number}: Option text must be a string") unless text.nil? || text.is_a?(String)

      correct = option["correct"].nil? ? false : option["correct"]
      errors.add(:base, "#{label}, option #{number}: Correct must be true or false") unless [ true, false ].include?(correct)

      { text: text.to_s, correct: correct == true }
    end
  end
end
EOF

require "test_helper"

class QuizExportTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    @quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Frontend Fest 2026")
  end

  test "writes the title and the questions with their options, in order" do
    add_question("Second", [ [ "B", true ], [ "C", false ] ], position_hint: :second)
    add_question("First", [ [ "A", false ], [ "D", true ] ], active: false)

    data = QuizExport.new(@quiz.reload).to_h

    assert_equal "Frontend Fest 2026", data[:title]
    assert_equal %w[Second First], data[:questions].map { |question| question[:text] }
    assert_equal [ true, false ], data[:questions].map { |question| question[:active] }
    assert_equal [ { text: "B", correct: true }, { text: "C", correct: false } ], data[:questions].first[:options]
  end

  test "writes exactly the keys of the format and nothing else" do
    add_question("Q", [ [ "A", true ], [ "B", false ] ])

    data = JSON.parse(QuizExport.new(@quiz.reload).pretty_json)

    assert_equal %w[questions title], data.keys.sort
    assert_equal %w[active options text], data["questions"].first.keys.sort
    assert_equal %w[correct text], data["questions"].first["options"].first.keys.sort
  end

  test "an empty quiz exports an empty list" do
    assert_equal({ title: "Frontend Fest 2026", questions: [] }, QuizExport.new(@quiz).to_h)
  end

  test "the pretty JSON is valid and matches the hash" do
    add_question("Q \"quoted\" <b>", [ [ "A", true ], [ "B", false ] ])
    json = QuizExport.new(@quiz.reload).pretty_json

    assert_includes json, "\n  \"title\": \"Frontend Fest 2026\""
    assert_equal QuizExport.new(@quiz.reload).to_h.deep_stringify_keys, JSON.parse(json)
  end

  private

  def add_question(text, rows, active: true, position_hint: nil)
    question = @quiz.questions.new(text: text, active: active)
    question.option_rows = rows.map { |option_text, correct| { text: option_text, correct: correct } }
    question.save!
    question
  end
end
EOF

require "test_helper"

class QuizImportTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  HTTP_JSON = <<~JSON.freeze
    {
      "title": "Frontend Fest 2026",
      "questions": [
        {
          "text": "Which HTTP status code means \\"Too Many Requests\\"?",
          "active": true,
          "options": [
            {"text": "418", "correct": false},
            {"text": "429", "correct": true}
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  JSON

  def import(json)
    QuizImport.new(json: json)
  end

  def assert_refused(json, *messages)
    import = import(json)
    assert_no_difference [ "Quiz.count", "Question.count", "Option.count" ] do
      assert_not import.save, "expected a refusal"
    end
    assert_nil import.quiz
    messages.each do |message|
      assert_includes import.errors.full_messages, message
    end
  end

  def document(questions: nil, title: "Talk", **extra)
    { "title" => title, "questions" => questions || [ question_hash ] }.merge(extra).to_json
  end

  def question_hash(text: "Q?", options: nil, **extra)
    { "text" => text, "options" => options || [ { "text" => "A", "correct" => true }, { "text" => "B", "correct" => false } ] }.merge(extra.stringify_keys)
  end

  test "imports the format from the issue, keeping the order" do
    import = import(HTTP_JSON)

    assert_difference "Quiz.count", 1 do
      assert import.save, import.errors.full_messages.inspect
    end

    quiz = import.quiz
    assert_equal "Frontend Fest 2026", quiz.title
    assert_equal [ 'Which HTTP status code means "Too Many Requests"?' ], quiz.questions.map(&:text)
    assert quiz.questions.first.active?
    assert_equal [ "418", "429" ], quiz.questions.first.options.map(&:text)
    assert_equal [ false, true ], quiz.questions.first.options.map(&:correct)
  end

  test "keeps the order of questions and options" do
    json = document(questions: [
      question_hash(text: "first", options: [ { "text" => "z", "correct" => false }, { "text" => "a", "correct" => true } ]),
      question_hash(text: "second")
    ])
    quiz = import(json).tap(&:save!).quiz

    assert_equal %w[first second], quiz.questions.map(&:text)
    assert_equal %w[z a], quiz.questions.first.options.map(&:text)
    assert_equal [ 1, 2 ], quiz.questions.map(&:position)
  end

  test "active defaults to true and correct defaults to false" do
    json = document(questions: [ { "text" => "Q", "options" => [ { "text" => "A" }, { "text" => "B", "correct" => true } ] } ])
    quiz = import(json).tap(&:save!).quiz

    assert quiz.questions.first.active?
    assert_equal [ false, true ], quiz.questions.first.options.map(&:correct)
  end

  test "active false keeps the question inactive" do
    json = document(questions: [ question_hash(active: false) ])
    quiz = import(json).tap(&:save!).quiz
    assert_not quiz.questions.first.active?
  end

  test "an import always creates a new quiz, even when the title exists" do
    existing = Quiz.create!(title: "Frontend Fest 2026")

    import = import(HTTP_JSON)
    assert_difference "Quiz.count", 1 do
      import.save!
    end
    assert_not_equal existing.id, import.quiz.id
    assert_equal 2, Quiz.where(title: "Frontend Fest 2026").count
  end

  test "text and title are trimmed like the forms do" do
    json = document(title: "  Padded  ", questions: [ question_hash(text: "  Q  ", options: [ { "text" => " A ", "correct" => true }, { "text" => "B" } ]) ])
    quiz = import(json).tap(&:save!).quiz

    assert_equal "Padded", quiz.title
    assert_equal "Q", quiz.questions.first.text
    assert_equal "A", quiz.questions.first.options.first.text
  end

  test "a quiz without questions can be imported" do
    quiz = import(document(questions: [])).tap(&:save!).quiz
    assert_equal 0, quiz.questions.count
  end

  test "blank option rows are skipped, like in the question form" do
    json = document(questions: [ question_hash(options: [
      { "text" => "", "correct" => true }, { "text" => "  " }, { "text" => "A", "correct" => true }, { "text" => "B" }, { "correct" => true }
    ]) ])
    quiz = import(json).tap(&:save!).quiz
    assert_equal %w[A B], quiz.questions.first.options.map(&:text)
  end

  test "several correct options are fine" do
    json = document(questions: [ question_hash(options: [ { "text" => "A", "correct" => true }, { "text" => "B", "correct" => true } ]) ])
    assert import(json).save
  end

  test "invalid JSON imports nothing" do
    assert_refused "{ \"title\": ", "Quiz JSON is not valid JSON"
  end

  test "blank input imports nothing" do
    assert_refused "  ", "Quiz JSON can't be blank"
    assert_refused nil, "Quiz JSON can't be blank"
  end

  test "a document that is not an object imports nothing" do
    assert_refused "[]", "Quiz JSON must be an object with \"title\" and \"questions\""
    assert_refused "null", "Quiz JSON must be an object with \"title\" and \"questions\""
  end

  test "a title is required" do
    assert_refused document(title: "  "), "Title can't be blank"
    assert_refused({ "questions" => [] }.to_json), "Title can't be blank"
  end

  test "a title must be text and at most 200 characters" do
    assert_refused document(title: 42), "Title must be a string"
    assert_refused document(title: "x" * 201), "Title is too long (maximum is 200 characters)"
  end

  test "questions must be a list" do
    assert_refused({ "title" => "Talk" }.to_json, "Questions must be a list")
    assert_refused document(questions: "nope"), "Questions must be a list"
  end

  test "a question must be an object" do
    assert_refused document(questions: [ "text" ]), "Question 1 must be an object"
  end

  test "a question needs text" do
    assert_refused document(questions: [ question_hash(text: " ") ]), "Question 1: Question can't be blank"
    assert_refused document(questions: [ { "options" => [ { "text" => "A", "correct" => true }, { "text" => "B" } ] } ]),
                   "Question 1: Question can't be blank"
  end

  test "question text must be a string" do
    assert_refused document(questions: [ question_hash(text: 5) ]), "Question 1: Question must be a string"
  end

  test "active must be true or false" do
    assert_refused document(questions: [ question_hash(active: "yes") ]), "Question 1: Active must be true or false"
    assert_refused document(questions: [ question_hash(active: 0) ]), "Question 1: Active must be true or false"
  end

  test "a question needs at least two options" do
    assert_refused document(questions: [ question_hash(options: [ { "text" => "Only", "correct" => true } ]) ]),
                   "Question 1: Add at least two options"
    assert_refused document(questions: [ question_hash(options: [ { "text" => "A", "correct" => true }, { "text" => "" } ]) ]),
                   "Question 1: Add at least two options"
  end

  test "a question needs one correct option" do
    assert_refused document(questions: [ question_hash(options: [ { "text" => "A" }, { "text" => "B", "correct" => false } ]) ]),
                   "Question 1: Mark at least one option as correct"
  end

  test "a blank option marked correct does not count" do
    assert_refused document(questions: [ question_hash(options: [ { "text" => "A" }, { "text" => " ", "correct" => true } ]) ]),
                   "Question 1: Mark at least one option as correct"
  end

  test "both option rules are reported together" do
    assert_refused document(questions: [ question_hash(options: [ { "text" => "A" } ]) ]),
                   "Question 1: Add at least two options",
                   "Question 1: Mark at least one option as correct"
  end

  test "options must be a list of objects with text and a boolean correct" do
    assert_refused document(questions: [ question_hash(options: "A, B") ]), "Question 1: Options must be a list"
    assert_refused document(questions: [ question_hash(options: [ { "text" => "A", "correct" => true }, "B" ]) ]),
                   "Question 1, option 2 must be an object"
    assert_refused document(questions: [ question_hash(options: [ { "text" => "A", "correct" => "true" }, { "text" => "B" } ]) ]),
                   "Question 1, option 1: Correct must be true or false"
    assert_refused document(questions: [ question_hash(options: [ { "text" => 418, "correct" => true }, { "text" => "B" } ]) ]),
                   "Question 1, option 1: Option text must be a string"
  end

  test "a bad question anywhere means nothing is imported, not even the good questions" do
    json = document(questions: [
      question_hash(text: "Good one"),
      question_hash(text: "Bad one", options: [ { "text" => "A" }, { "text" => "B" } ])
    ])
    assert_refused json, "Question 2: Mark at least one option as correct"
    assert_equal 0, Quiz.where(title: "Talk").count
  end

  test "errors name the question they belong to" do
    json = document(questions: [ question_hash, question_hash(text: "", options: []) ])
    import = import(json)
    assert_not import.save
    assert_includes import.errors.full_messages, "Question 2: Question can't be blank"
    assert_includes import.errors.full_messages, "Question 2: Add at least two options"
    assert_not_includes import.errors.full_messages.join, "Question 1"
  end

  test "unknown keys are ignored" do
    json = { "id" => 99, "title" => "Talk", "exported_at" => "now",
             "questions" => [ { "text" => "Q", "position" => 7, "options" => [ { "text" => "A", "correct" => true, "id" => 3 }, { "text" => "B" } ] } ] }.to_json
    assert import(json).save
  end

  test "round trip: exporting and importing again gives the same quiz" do
    source = Quiz.create!(title: "Source")
    first = source.questions.new(text: "First", active: false)
    first.option_rows = [ { text: "x", correct: false }, { text: "y", correct: true } ]
    first.save!
    second = source.questions.new(text: "Second", active: true)
    second.option_rows = [ { text: "p", correct: true }, { text: "q", correct: true } ]
    second.save!

    copy = import(QuizExport.new(source.reload).pretty_json).tap(&:save!).quiz

    assert_equal "Source", copy.title
    assert_not_equal source.id, copy.id
    assert_equal QuizExport.new(source.reload).to_h, QuizExport.new(copy.reload).to_h
  end
end

require "test_helper"

class ImportExportTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    @auth = moderator_headers
    @quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Frontend Fest 2026")
    question = @quiz.questions.new(text: 'Which HTTP status code means "Too Many Requests"?', active: true)
    question.option_rows = [ { text: "418", correct: false }, { text: "429", correct: true } ]
    question.save!
  end

  def basic(user, password)
    { "HTTP_AUTHORIZATION" => ActionController::HttpAuthentication::Basic.encode_credentials(user, password) }
  end

  def valid_json(title: "Imported talk")
    {
      title: title,
      questions: [
        { text: "Q1?", active: true, options: [ { text: "A", correct: false }, { text: "B", correct: true } ] }
      ]
    }.to_json
  end

  test "the quiz page links to its export" do
    get "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}", headers: @auth
    assert_response :success
    assert_select "a[href=?]", "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/export", text: "Export"
  end

  test "the export page shows the quiz as JSON in the only pre element" do
    get "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/export", headers: @auth
    assert_response :success
    assert_select "pre", count: 1

    data = JSON.parse(css_select("pre").first.text)
    assert_equal({
      "title" => "Frontend Fest 2026",
      "questions" => [ {
        "text" => 'Which HTTP status code means "Too Many Requests"?',
        "active" => true,
        "options" => [ { "text" => "418", "correct" => false }, { "text" => "429", "correct" => true } ]
      } ]
    }, data)
  end

  test "the export page is only reachable with the moderator's credentials" do
    get "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/export"
    assert_response :unauthorized
    get "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/export", headers: basic("moderator", "wrong")
    assert_response :unauthorized
  end

  test "the import form is only reachable with the moderator's credentials" do
    get "/moderate/import/new"
    assert_response :unauthorized
    post "/moderate/import", params: { quiz_import: { json: valid_json } }
    assert_response :unauthorized
    assert_equal 1, Quiz.count
  end

  test "the quiz list has an Import quiz button that opens the import form" do
    get "/moderate", headers: @auth
    assert_select "form[action=?] button", "/moderate/import/new", text: "Import quiz"

    get "/moderate/import/new", headers: @auth
    assert_response :success
    assert_select "label", text: "Quiz JSON"
    assert_select "textarea[name=?]", "quiz_import[json]"
    assert_select "input[type=submit], button", text: "Import"
  end

  test "a valid import creates a new quiz and opens its page" do
    assert_difference [ "Quiz.count", "Question.count", "Option.count" ], +1, +1, +2 do
      post "/moderate/import", params: { quiz_import: { json: valid_json } }, headers: @auth
    end
    quiz = Quiz.find_by!(title: "Imported talk")
    assert_redirected_to "/moderate/quizzes/#{quiz.id}"
    assert_equal "Quiz imported.", flash[:notice]
  end

  test "importing a quiz whose title already exists still creates a new one" do
    assert_difference "Quiz.count", 1 do
      post "/moderate/import", params: { quiz_import: { json: valid_json(title: "Frontend Fest 2026") } }, headers: @auth
    end
    assert_equal 2, Quiz.where(title: "Frontend Fest 2026").count
  end

  test "an invalid import shows the errors and creates nothing" do
    broken = { title: "Half done", questions: [
      { text: "Fine", options: [ { text: "A", correct: true }, { text: "B" } ] },
      { text: "Broken", options: [ { text: "A" }, { text: "B" } ] }
    ] }.to_json

    assert_no_difference [ "Quiz.count", "Question.count", "Option.count" ] do
      post "/moderate/import", params: { quiz_import: { json: broken } }, headers: @auth
    end
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity
    assert_select "[role=alert] li", text: "Question 2: Mark at least one option as correct"
    assert_select "textarea", text: /Half done/
  end

  test "invalid JSON is refused with an error and nothing is created" do
    assert_no_difference "Quiz.count" do
      post "/moderate/import", params: { quiz_import: { json: "{ nope" } }, headers: @auth
    end
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity
    assert_select "[role=alert] li", text: "Quiz JSON is not valid JSON"
  end

  test "a request without the form field is a bad request" do
    post "/moderate/import", params: {}, headers: @auth
    assert_response :bad_request
  end

  test "exporting and importing gives back the same quiz" do
    get "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/export", headers: @auth
    exported = css_select("pre").first.text

    post "/moderate/import", params: { quiz_import: { json: exported } }, headers: @auth
    copy = Quiz.order(:id).last
    assert_not_equal @quiz.id, copy.id
    assert_equal QuizExport.new(@quiz.reload).to_h, QuizExport.new(copy).to_h
  end
end
EOF

require "application_system_test_case"

class ImportExportTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  QUESTION_TEXT = "Which HTTP status code means \"Too Many Requests\"?".freeze

  IMPORT_JSON = <<~JSON.freeze
    {
      "title": "Frontend Fest 2026",
      "questions": [
        {
          "text": "Which HTTP status code means \\"Too Many Requests\\"?",
          "active": true,
          "options": [
            {"text": "418", "correct": false},
            {"text": "429", "correct": true}
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  JSON

  setup do
    @quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Frontend Fest 2026")
    question = @quiz.questions.new(text: QUESTION_TEXT, active: true)
    question.option_rows = [ { text: "418", correct: false }, { text: "429", correct: true } ]
    question.save!
  end

  test "the export page shows the quiz as JSON ready to copy" do
    visit "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}"
    click_link "Export"

    assert_selector "h1", text: "Export"
    assert_selector "pre", count: 1
    data = JSON.parse(find("pre").text)
    assert_equal "Frontend Fest 2026", data["title"]
    assert_equal [ QUESTION_TEXT ], data["questions"].map { |question| question["text"] }
    assert_equal [ false, true ], data["questions"].first["options"].map { |option| option["correct"] }
  end

  test "import quiz from the quiz list creates a new quiz and opens it" do
    visit "/moderate"
    click_button "Import quiz"

    fill_in "Quiz JSON", with: IMPORT_JSON
    click_button "Import"

    assert_selector "h1", text: "Frontend Fest 2026"
    assert_selector ".question-item", text: QUESTION_TEXT
    assert_equal 2, Quiz.where(title: "Frontend Fest 2026").count
  end

  test "a broken import shows the errors, imports nothing and keeps the text" do

    assert_text "Question 1: Mark at least one option as correct"
    assert_field "Quiz JSON", with: broken
    assert_equal 1, Quiz.count
  end

  test "invalid JSON is refused" do
    visit "/moderate/import/new"
    fill_in "Quiz JSON", with: "{ \"title\": "
    click_button "Import"

    assert_text "Quiz JSON is not valid JSON"
    assert_equal 1, Quiz.count
  end

  test "what the export page shows imports back as the same quiz" do
    visit "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/export"
    exported = find("pre").text

    visit "/moderate/import/new"

    assert_selector ".question-item", text: QUESTION_TEXT
    assert_equal 2, Quiz.count
  end

  test "the export page fits a phone screen without sideways scrolling" do
    page.current_window.resize_to(390, 844)
    visit "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/export"
    assert_selector "pre"
    overflow = page.evaluate_script("document.documentElement.scrollWidth - document.documentElement.clientWidth")
    assert_operator overflow, :<=, 0, "export page is #{overflow}px wider than the phone screen"
  end
end

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat > docs/quiz-json-format.md <<'EOF'
# Quiz JSON: export and import

Moderators move a quiz to another conference, or share it with a colleague who
runs Quizzy too, as JSON:

- **Export**: the quiz page's "Export" link opens `/moderate/quizzes/:id/export`,
  which shows the quiz as JSON inside the page's only `<pre>`, ready to copy.
- **Import quiz**: the "Import quiz" button on `/moderate` opens
  `/moderate/import/new` with a "Quiz JSON" text area and the "Import" button.
  `POST /moderate/import` creates a **new** quiz (even if one with the same title
  exists) and opens its page with "Quiz imported.".

## Format

```json
{
  "title": "Frontend Fest 2026",
  "questions": [
    {
      "text": "Which HTTP status code means \"Too Many Requests\"?",
      "active": true,
      "options": [
        {"text": "418", "correct": false},
        {"text": "429", "correct": true}
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Export writes exactly these keys, in this order, and nothing else (no ids, no
timestamps, no positions): the quiz `title`, then its `questions` (all of them,
inactive ones included), each with `text`, `active` and `options`, and each option
with `text` and `correct`. Questions and options keep their order. An empty quiz
exports `"questions": []`.

## Import rules

The document is checked completely before anything is written. The quiz and its
questions are saved in one transaction, so a document that breaks a rule creates
nothing: not the quiz, not part of its questions. The error page lists every
problem it found, each question's problems prefixed with the question number.

- `title`: required, trimmed, at most 200 characters (the quiz form's rule).
  Messages: "Title can't be blank", "Title must be a string".
- `questions`: required list (`[]` is fine). Message: "Questions must be a list".
- `text` of a question: required, trimmed (the question form's rule). Message:
  "Question N: Question can't be blank".
- `active`: optional, `true` by default. Must be `true` or `false`.
- `options`: required list. Message: "Question N: Options must be a list".
- Option `text`: a string. Rows whose text is blank after trimming are skipped,
  even if marked correct (the question form's rule).
- Option `correct`: optional, `false` by default. Must be `true` or `false`.
- After skipping blank rows, a question needs at least two options ("Question N:
  Add at least two options") and at least one correct option ("Question N: Mark at
  least one option as correct"). Both can show together. Several correct options
  are fine.
- `null` counts as missing (so `"active": null` means the default).
- Keys other than these are ignored, so an export from a newer version still
  imports.
- Invalid JSON, or a top level that is not an object: "Quiz JSON is not valid
  JSON" / "Quiz JSON must be an object with "title" and "questions"".

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# Creates a brand-new quiz from the JSON that QuizExport writes ("Import quiz").
# An import always creates a quiz, even if one with the same title exists.
#
# Format (keys other than these are ignored):
#
#   { "title": "...",
#     "questions": [ { "text": "...", "active": true,
#                      "options": [ { "text": "...", "correct": false } ] } ] }
#
# "active" defaults to true and "correct" to false; null counts as missing.
#
# The whole document is checked before anything is written, and the quiz and its
# questions are saved in one transaction. A document that breaks a rule creates
# nothing: not the quiz, not part of its questions. Each question is checked by
# the same model rules as the question form (Question#option_rows).
class QuizImport
  include ActiveModel::Model

  attr_accessor :json
  attr_reader :quiz

The work is complete and verified. I'll make the final call that submits the work. The summary is above; nothing else follows the submit command.

Summary of what I delivered in `/app`:

**Repo state.** The repo already had the moderator release (quizzes, questions, ordering, preview), so I built the import/export on top of it rather than creating an app from scratch.

**Export**
- The quiz page has an "Export" link to `/moderate/quizzes/:id/export`.
- The page shows the quiz as pretty-printed JSON in the only `<pre>` on the page (`class="code-block"`).
- The JSON contains exactly the title and the questions (text, active, options with text and correct), in order, including inactive questions.

**Import**
- `/moderate` has an "Import quiz" button that opens `/moderate/import/new`, with a "Quiz JSON" text area and an "Import" button.
- `POST /moderate/import` always creates a new quiz, then redirects to its page with "Quiz imported.".
- The whole document is checked before anything is written. The quiz and its questions are saved in one transaction, so a refused import leaves no rows.
- Each question is checked by the same `Question` model rules the form uses, so the two cannot drift. Errors name the question, e.g. "Question 2: Add at least two options".
- A refused import returns 422 with the error list, and the typed JSON stays in the text area.

**Decisions where the spec was silent**
- `null` counts as missing, so `"active": null` means true and `"correct": null` means false.
- Extra keys are ignored, so an export from a newer version still imports.
- `title`, `questions`, `options`, and question `text` are required. Wrong types (e.g. a number as option text) are refused with a message.

**Verification**
- 79 unit and integration tests and 26 system tests pass. The new tests cover export shape, import rules, all-or-nothing behaviour, the round trip, auth, and browser flows at desktop and phone widths.
- Rubocop reports no offenses. Brakeman's scan reports 0 warnings.
- `bin/brakeman` exits 5 here only because its `--ensure-latest` check can't reach the network. `bin/bundler-audit` also needs GitHub, so it can't run offline.
- I started the app with `bin/serve` in production mode. `/up` returns 200, and `/moderate` without credentials returns 401. Over HTTP, the export `<pre>` parses to the expected keys, a broken import returns 422 and creates nothing, and a valid import redirects to the new quiz.
- I stopped the server, and removed the test data and build artifacts (production and development SQLite files, `public/assets`, logs), so `bin/serve` starts fresh.

**Docs.** `docs/quiz-json-format.md` holds the format and rules. `docs/design-notes.md` has the routes, labels, and decisions, and the README links to the format doc.

The changes are uncommitted in the working tree.
